title: Formatting from Python
summary: Make a report look finished: bold headers with Font, coloured cells with PatternFill, number formats like "#,##0.00", column widths, and a frozen header row. Formatting is set cell by cell, so loops do the work.
objectives: Make a header row bold with Font(bold=True).
Colour cells with PatternFill, based on their values.
Set number formats and column widths.
Freeze the header row with freeze_panes.

slides.h: By the end: a report the boss can read
slides.say: A sheet of plain numbers is hard to read. By the end of this lesson your program bolds the header, shows money with two decimals, colours the items that ran out and freezes the top row.
points: Widths and freezing live on the sheet.
p: A sheet of plain numbers is hard to read. By the end of this lesson your program bolds the header, shows money with two decimals, colours the items that ran out and freezes the top row.
Widths and freezing live on the sheet.

visual.text:
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("stock.xlsx")
ws = wb["Stock"]
ws["D1"] = "Value"
for r in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
    ws.cell(row=r, column=4, value=ws.cell(row=r, column=2).value * ws.cell(row=r, column=3).value)
for cell in ws[1]:
    cell.font = Font(bold=True)
for r in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
    ws.cell(row=r, column=4).number_format = "#,##0.00"
    if ws.cell(row=r, column=2).value == 0:
        ws.cell(row=r, column=1).fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFC7CE")
ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 16
ws.freeze_panes = "A2"
wb.save("stock_report.xlsx")

slides.say: `Font(bold=True)` and `PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFC7CE")` come from `openpyxl.styles`. Colours are hex codes, as in Excel’s “More colours”.
points: `ws[1]` is row 1: loop over it to style every header cell.
`fgColor` is the fill colour; "solid" makes it fill the cell.
Light red FFC7CE, light green C6EFCE, light yellow FFEB9C: Excel’s own warning colours.

tasks.prompt: From **marks.xlsx** (sheet **Marks**), save **marks_marked.xlsx** where row 1 is bold, and every **Maths** mark below 40 has the fill **FFC7CE** and every Maths mark of 75 or more the fill **C6EFCE**. Print how many were coloured, like **3 coloured**.
tasks.model:
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("marks.xlsx")
ws = wb["Marks"]
for cell in ws[1]:
    cell.font = Font(bold=True)
n = 0
for r in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
    c = ws.cell(row=r, column=2)
    if c.value < 40:
        c.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFC7CE")
        n += 1
    elif c.value >= 75:
        c.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="C6EFCE")
        n += 1
wb.save("marks_marked.xlsx")
print(f"{n} coloured")
